sentences.text: This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 26.11.2020 passed by II MACT, Kukshi, district Dhar in Claim Case No.36/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal, whereby learned tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.8,08,000/- to the appellants along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 12.2.2018.
2. Facts of the case are that Krishna Bhilala aged 25 years met with an accident on 18.4.2017 and succumbed.
3. Since only amount of compensation is disputed and the date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute, therefore it is not required to give vivid details.

Break-up of the amount awarded by the tribunal is as under :-
 towards medical bills Rs.1,22,
 for special diet, attender and conveyance Rs.11,00  towards loss of estate Rs.15,00  towards loss of consortium Rs.40,00  towards funeral expenses Rs.15,00  towards future loss of income Rs.6,04,800/- (Rs.
 =Rs.24000+40%x18)
 2  3.

Counsel for appellants submits that learned tribunal has assessed the income of deceased @
Rs.100/- per day ie. Rs.3000/- per month which is on lower side. Atleast minimum wages should have been awarded as per circular issued from the Labour Department of Govt. of M.P..

As per Saraswati vs Shyamlal on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83057782/
1 circular, on the date of accident, the income of the deceased should have been taken as Rs.7,125/-.

1 circular
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that survivors are wife, 2 minor sons and mother and father of the deceased, therefore all of them have to be awarded Rs.40,000/- each as consortium.
Hence prayed for enhancement of the awarded amount.

4. On the other hand, counsel for the Insurance Company vehementally opposed the prayer supporting the finding with regard to income of the deceased as arrived at by the Claims Tribunal and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

It is not in dispute that that where income of the deceased/victim is not established, and has to be assessed based on the facts and circumstances and evidence of the case, it is always safe to take resort to the circular issued under Minimum Wages Act.
It is not in dispute that on the date of accident ie.. 18.4.2017 minimum wages for the unskilled labourer was fixed as Rs.7,125/-.
No contrary evidence with regard to income of the deceased is available on record, therefore, in view of this Court, the income of deceased ought to have been taken as Rs.7,125/- per month.
Further adding 40% towards future prospects and after deduction of 1/3rd amount towards personal expenses, the loss of dependency comes to Rs.14,36,000/-.
Under head loss of estate and funeral expenses, a sum of Rs.16,500/-in each head ought to have been awarded.
Further, towards loss of consortium to all the four appellants, a sum of Rs.1,76,000/- (Rs.44000x4) should have been awarded.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified as under:
3 MA-573-2021 HEAD AMOUNT towards medical bills Rs.1,22,123/-
for special diet, attender and conveyance Rs.11,000/-
 towards loss of estate Rs.16,
 towards loss of consortium Rs.1,7  towards funeral expenses Rs.16,
 towards future loss of income Rs.14,36,400/- (Rs  Rs.1,19,700/- x  -------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------
 total Rs.17  =========================== ============
7.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.17,78,523/- instead of Rs.8,08,000/-.
Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.9,70,523/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the tribunal.
8. Appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.6 Lacs and paid the court fee accordingly.

However, for the remaining amount of Rs.3,70,523/- the court fee shall be paid by the Saraswati vs Shyamlal on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83057782/
2 appellants within a period of 60 days from the date of the order of this Court and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance company upto a period of three months, the appellants/claimants shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
9. In the result, the appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation to the extent indicated above.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE MK 4 MA-573-2021 Saraswati vs Shyamlal on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83057782/
